history.summary: IDENTITY PARTIALLY VERIFIED: onefivenine locality listings document two Shiva shrines in Kolasib town (PIN 796081) - 'Kalasiva Mandir' and 'Shiv Mandir' at Hmar Veng, Kolasib, plus a separate 'Shiv Mandir' at NH 54, Saidan, Kolasib - and onefivenine's Kolasib District page calls 'kolasib shiv mandir' the famous temple of Kolasib district. It is unclear whether the two Hmar Veng listings are the same shrine under variant spellings ('Kalasiva' vs 'Shiva') or two distinct temples, and no listing gives founding dates, patronage, or timings, so the Hmar Veng pair is taken as the best-supported referent for this record; treat as provisional pending local confirmation. Coordinates are for the Hmar Veng locality, not the shrine itself (verify). Do not conflate with the well-documented Lakshmi Narayan Mandir at Chanmari West (Vaishnavite, separate record) or the Shiv Mandirs of Aizawl.

town_description: Kolasib is the district headquarters of Kolasib district in northern Mizoram, about 66 km south of Aizawl on NH 54 (PIN 796081). A market and transport town on the Aizawl-Assam route, it is overwhelmingly Christian (Mizo Presbyterian majority), with a small Hindu minority - mostly non-Mizo traders, government staff and paramilitary personnel - that maintains the town's few community temples.

travel.railway: Bairabi railway station is the railhead in Kolasib district (verify distance to Kolasib town).
travel.road: Approx. 66 km from Aizawl via NH 54; regular buses and shared sumos on the Aizawl-Silchar route.
